claims.claim: Eyring rate arithmetic implements the activation-free-energy equation.
claims.convention: k=κkBT/h exp(-ΔG‡/RT); κ=1; absolute ΔG in kcal/mol, T inK; first-order units.
claims.limitations: Equation correctness does not identify a physical barrier or establish transition-state assumptions.
claims.method: 75-digit Decimal equation on frozen f32 inputs over temperature/barrier grid.
claims.result: Normal-rate subset maximum relative error 6.9231e-8; subnormal and extreme failures separately retained.
claims.source: IUPAC Green Book (2008/2012), pp.45–46,65–67: https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IUPAC-GB3-2012-2ndPrinting-PDFsearchable.pdf; NIST CODATA2022: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Table/allascii.txt

claims.claim: Physical constants and kcal/Hartree conversion are accurate.
claims.convention: kB/h/NA exact SI; R=kBNA/4184; Hartree energy fromCODATA.
claims.limitations: Numerical effects generally smaller than f32 rounding; physical energy-model errors not tested by constants.
claims.method: Independent Decimal arithmetic from primary constants.
claims.result: R truncation relative difference ≈3.22e-10; Hartree conversion difference ≈2.03e-10 kcal mol^-1 Hartree^-1.

claims.claim: Zero ΔΔG gives equal R:S and reversing sign exchanges preference.
claims.convention: ΔΔG=G‡S−G‡R, common reactant and equal pathway prefactors; zero→50:50.
claims.limitations: This algebraic convention cannot infer the absolute enantiomer from unsigned experimental ee.
claims.method: Independent two-pathway rates with common energy shift, signed grid and signed zero.
claims.result: R/S max error 3.7596e-6 percentage points; zero and sign symmetry observed.

claims.claim: Enantiomeric excess arithmetic follows the two-pathway populations.
claims.convention: Absolute ee=100|pR−pS|; signed ee, if requested, must retain configuration convention.
claims.limitations: Finite precision saturation is not experimentally complete selectivity.
claims.method: Independent pathway probabilities, zero and small/large differences.
claims.result: Max absolute error 7.5191e-6 percentage points; tiny ee and minority populations can round to zero.

claims.claim: simulate can output an absolute rate from the same ΔΔG used for selectivity.
claims.convention: A difference fixes a rate ratio, not either absolute activation barrier.
claims.limitations: The standalone rate function is correct when supplied an actual absolute barrier; the interface is the problem.
claims.method: Two barrier pairs(10,11) and(20,21) have same difference but different rates; frozen CLI observation.

claims.basis: Audit of the accepted numerical domain, not an assertion that documentation promises finite outputs for every finite input.
claims.claim: Rate and selectivity calculations have a defined finite numerical domain.
claims.convention: Finite input can map outside representable output range; this must be reported.
claims.limitations: This is a bounded precision/validation claim, not evidence that ordinary barriers have chemically material errors.
claims.method: Large positive/negative barriers, temperature extremes, NaN/infinity and zero-temperature inputs.
claims.result: Wider grid includes 16 rate underflows and 15 nonfinite rates; CLI checks inputs only.
claims.source: IUPAC Green Book (2008/2012), pp.45–46,65–67: https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IUPAC-GB3-2012-2ndPrinting-PDFsearchable.pdf; IEEE754 f32 range

claims.claim: MMFF ensemble weights use the normalized Boltzmann equation.
claims.convention: wi∝exp(-(Ei−Emin)/(RT)); kcal/mol; positive temperature; unit degeneracy.
claims.limitations: Mocked optimizer results do not validate search completeness or MMFF energies as thermodynamic free energies.
claims.method: Controlled energy/status injection into frozen routine; independent Decimal weights for single/equal/two/three/offset/extreme/temperature/window cases.
claims.result: Maximum population error 1.9429e-16 in isolated weighting tests.

claims.basis: Audit of a possible stronger reading of “optimized”; the frozen code retains optimizer status and does not explicitly promise convergence of every retained state.
claims.claim: Calling the retained MMFF ensemble fully optimized implies that its conformers converged.
claims.convention: Return status 0 means converged; finite nonzero status may still be unconverged.
claims.limitations: Do not confuse retaining an unconverged state with a proven material descriptor error; magnitude depends on that geometry.
claims.method: Inject status −1/0/1 and nonfinite energies; inspect retained IDs/statuses.
claims.result: Status 1 is retained and weighted; negative status and nonfinite energy are excluded.
claims.source: RDKit installed2026.3.4 MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs docstring and official https://www.rdkit.org/docs/source/rdkit.Chem.rdForceFieldHelpers.html

claims.claim: CREST populations correspond to configured QuantumConfig.temperature_k.
claims.convention: Population temperature must equal requested T; external table temperature cannot be assumed.
claims.limitations: Direct frozen helper/command audit; no actual external CREST execution is claimed.
claims.method: Frozen realistic two-state summary at 298.15 K, requested 500 K; independently evaluate weights.
claims.result: Population error 0.1116127958 at 500 K; command omits --temp and parsed table bypasses recomputation.
claims.source: CREST official --temp documentation and frozen v2.12 cregen.f90: https://crest-lab.github.io/crest-docs/page/documentation/keywords.html; IUPAC Green Book (2008/2012), pp.45–46,65–67: https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IUPAC-GB3-2012-2ndPrinting-PDFsearchable.pdf

claims.claim: CREST missing-table fallback correctly weights supplied electronic energies.
claims.convention: Convert Hartree differences to kcal/mol, subtract minimum, normalize atconfigured T.
claims.limitations: Degeneracy defaults to one and electronic energies are not state free energies; missing/incorrect degeneracies change expected populations.
claims.method: Frozen two-frame energy input at 298.15/500 K, independent Hartree conversion.
claims.result: Maximum population error≈1.03e-12, including coordinate-comment energy rounding.
claims.source: IUPAC Green Book (2008/2012), pp.45–46,65–67: https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IUPAC-GB3-2012-2ndPrinting-PDFsearchable.pdf; NIST CODATA2022: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Table/allascii.txt

claims.claim: Parsed CREST weights are valid nonnegative probabilities.
claims.convention: Each population ≥0; positive finite normalization total.
claims.limitations: Malformed-table validation test; does not assert real CREST normally emits negative populations.
claims.method: Synthetic malformed population table with weights −0.5,1.5.
claims.result: Helper accepts negative population because only finiteness and sum>0 checked.

claims.claim: Native supplied conformer weights correctly average Sterimol descriptors.
claims.convention: Normalize supplied nonnegative weights then Σwi di; Å; preserve ensemble extrema/count.
claims.limitations: Does not establish the supplied weights are thermodynamically justified.
claims.method: Native frozen CLI on an analytic XYZ pair; independent packed-record decoding.
claims.result: Accepted cases max descriptor error 2.6703e-7 Å; 1:3 supplied weights give L=5.2, B1=1.7, B5=4.97.

claims.basis: Stronger Boltzmann interpretation tested by the audit; the function itself explicitly implements a uniform fallback when weights are absent.
claims.claim: Missing weights with supplied conformer energies produce Boltzmann populations.
claims.convention: Energy-derived populations require an explicit equation and T; uniform averaging follows equal state weights.
claims.limitations: Uniform fallback is explicit implementation behavior; documentation must not describe all native averages as energy-derived.
claims.method: Native parse CSV with unequal energies 0;1 and missing weights.
claims.result: Native path uses a uniform average, L=4.7 Å, irrespective of energies; differs from a Boltzmann expectation.

claims.basis: Validation behavior tested by the audit, not a quoted promise of partial-ensemble renormalization.
claims.claim: Missing or invalid native conformer geometry does not silently produce a partial ensemble.
claims.convention: Reject an incomplete ensemble or explicitly track excluded population; avoid silent partial results.
claims.limitations: Python preparation intentionally filters some failed energies; these are distinct stage semantics.
claims.method: A missing file and a malformed XYZ as the second conformer.
claims.result: Both return errors and no packed record; the native path does not silently discard the bad conformer.

claims.claim: Buried-volume ensemble weightedmeans implement normalized sums.
claims.convention: Use the same populations for each scalar; treat extrema and conformer-identity reductions separately.
claims.limitations: Tiny/huge weight normalization and NaN parameters are separate failures; no complete chemical ensemble claim.
claims.method: One/two/three/nonunit/permuted analytic descriptors versus Decimal.
claims.result: Maximum weighted-mean error 6.3578e-7 Å³.

claims.claim: Positive finite weights can be normalized independent of common scale.
claims.convention: Multiplying all weightsby any positive finite factor should not change valid probabilities when representable.
claims.limitations: Ordinary normalized weights are unaffected; a correction should rescale before summation.
claims.method: Compare weights 1:3 with 1e-10:3e-10; also test sum overflow.
claims.result: A valid tiny-weight ratio is rejected as zero total; a large finite sum can overflow.

claims.basis: Public-API domain/validation test; no evidence that the ordinary validated CLI supplies NaN descriptors.
claims.claim: Public buried-volume aggregation has a scientifically defined result for accepted inputs.
claims.convention: Nonfinite components require an error or an explicit missing-data meaning.
claims.limitations: Direct API finding; normal CLI geometry validation may prevent this input.
claims.method: Direct frozen public API: NaN descriptor with weight 1.
claims.result: Returns Ok with NaN vbur_boltz; exact nonfinite output preserved.

claims.claim: Stored conformer energy_span is maximum minus minimum.
claims.convention: Energy span=max(E)−min(E); alternatively require relative energies to have minimum zero.
claims.limitations: When relative energies are correctly referenced to the minimum, max equals max-minus-min.
claims.method: Accepted native CSV energies [1,2], independently decode the packed record.
claims.result: Stored span is 2 instead of 1; code uses max and does not require minimum zero.

claims.claim: ee-to-ΔΔG conversion reproduces the standard magnitude equation.
claims.limitations: Requires kinetic selectivity assumptions; absolute value intentionally discards enantiomer identity.
claims.method: Independent equation for validpositive/negative ee and two temperatures.
claims.result: Valid interior inputs agree within floating-point precision.

claims.basis: Mathematical interpretation of an implemented clipping behavior; no measured detection limit was supplied.
claims.claim: 100% and out-of-range ee can be converted to a finite exact barrier.
claims.convention: 100% is an infinite mathematical limit; >100% is invalid; censored measurements require bounds.
claims.limitations: If clipping represents a detection limit, report the assumption and lower bound instead of an exact observation.
claims.method: Cases ±100/±101 versus the analytic limit/domain.
claims.result: All are clipped to 99.999%, giving finite 7.231911... kcal/mol at 298.15 K without censoring metadata.

claims.claim: Ni-hDA stored targets use their recorded 298.15 K temperature.
claims.convention: Experimental 80 °C, use 353.15 K (allow original rounded R).
claims.limitations: Do not silently recompute targets; preserve published values and correct provenance separately.
claims.method: Independent reverse conversion of all 11 labeled source pairs.
claims.result: Ten pairs imply 353.113701 K instead of 298.15 K; maximum room-temperature target difference ≈0.333685 kcal/mol.
claims.source: Corrected primary Ni-hDA SI Table S3; primary author CSV; NIST CODATA2022: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Table/allascii.txt

claims.claim: Ni-hDA ID2064 target and ee are mutually consistent.
claims.confidence: High confidence in the inconsistency; uncertain which datum is correct
claims.convention: Use the same temperature and selectivity equation for each row.
claims.limitations: The disagreement exists upstream too; resolution requires author/experimental records.
claims.method: Independently convert 3% ee at 353.15 K and infer T from the published target.
claims.result: Source 3% ee and target ≈0.028072 correspond to ≈2% ee at 353 K; implied T=235.37 K.
claims.source: Corrected primary Ni-hDA Table S3 and frozen author CSV

claims.basis: Experimental interpretation tested for evidentiary support, not a claim that the README explicitly asserts measured conformer populations.
claims.claim: Population-weighted steric descriptors establish experimental conformer populations.
claims.convention: True equilibrium populations depend on appropriate free energies, state counts, solvent and temperature.
claims.limitations: MMFF/xTB electronic-energy weighting and finite conformer search remain model assumptions.
claims.method: Assess energy sources, degeneracy assumptions and failed-conformer handling against statistical thermodynamics.
claims.result: Numerical weights are verified conditionally; no independent experimental population measurements were supplied.
